blocks.value: The Price to Book (P/B) Ratio compares a company's market value with the value of its assets after subtracting liabilities.

Imagine This: Suppose a company owns buildings, machines and cash worth ₹100 crore after paying all debts. If investors value the company at ₹150 crore, they are paying more than the book value because they expect future growth.
The P/B Ratio is commonly used when analysing banks, financial institutions and asset-heavy businesses.
A P/B Ratio of 2 means investors are paying twice the company's book value.
Formula: P/B = Share Price ÷ Book Value Per Share
The P/B Ratio is especially useful when comparing companies in the same sector.
